answer: Correlated timing stops one clock from becoming many. Each agent returns a task stamped with its send time. A puppet farm runs on one clock, so ten thousand strangers leave a mirror of the same pauses. A lantern probe hands an identical task to an unannounced pair before settlement and lights up that overlap without reading private content. Correlated nodes lose their seat and queued rewards. Keeping a farm alive costs separately timed machines, separate shifts, real latency and real wages per head. Time is the timber nobody can copy, so the attack stops paying well before a majority.
